name: :has() Sibling Dim Spotlight
description: Hovering any item in a grid dims every sibling and lifts the focused one, a focus-spotlight interaction built with pure CSS and no JavaScript.
usage: Drop styles.css into your stylesheet and wrap focusable cards in a .spotlight-grid using the markup from index.html. Hover or keyboard-focus any .spotlight-card and its siblings dim while it lifts — no script required.
license: LogRocket Blog article — code snippets free to reuse; reimplemented cleanly. :has() is native Baseline CSS.

name: 3D Tilt Card
description: A card that lifts and tilts in 3D perspective on hover, with inner layers floating at different depths and a sheen sweep.
usage: Wrap the card in .scs-tilt (sets perspective). Inner content gets .scs-tilt__layer plus a depth class; tune the rotateX/rotateY and translateZ values to taste.

name: Animated Details Accordion
description: A native, accessible accordion that smoothly animates open and closed from height 0 to auto using the details element with zero JavaScript.
usage: Copy styles.css and the markup from index.html, then give every <details> in a group the same name attribute for exclusive (one-open-at-a-time) behaviour. Add the open attribute to whichever panel should start expanded.
license: Builder.io blog article — code shared for reuse; details/::details-content are native HTML/CSS. Reimplemented cleanly.

name: Animated Gradient Mesh
description: A living, slowly-shifting multi-color radial-gradient mesh background driven entirely by CSS keyframes.
usage: Wrap your section in a .scs-mesh element. The mesh fills the container; give the container a height (or use it full-screen) and place your content inside.

name: Animated Text Gradient
description: A headline filled with a slowly drifting multi-stop gradient for a premium, living-color title with no JS.
usage: Copy styles.css into your stylesheet and add the .animated-gradient-text class to any heading. Tune angle, size, speed, and color stops via the --atg-* custom properties (inline or in CSS).
license: web.dev article (Adam Argyle), content under CC-BY 4.0; technique is native CSS — reimplemented

name: Aurora Background
description: Soft northern-lights glow blobs that slowly drift, scale, and fade behind your content.
usage: Wrap content in .scs-aurora and include the .scs-aurora__lights layer with its four spans. Give the wrapper a height; content sits above the aurora automatically.

name: Auto-Invert Difference Cursor
description: A custom circular cursor that auto-inverts whatever it passes over using mix-blend-mode: difference, so it stays legible on any background.
usage: Link styles.css, drop the single .scs-difference-cursor element on the page, then paste the script that feeds --x/--y position and toggles state classes; add .scs-cursor-target to any element you want the cursor to grow over (native links/buttons are auto-detected).
license: Public-domain CSS idiom — mix-blend-mode is native CSS; reimplemented cleanly from the CSS-Tricks concept.

name: Container-Query Adaptive Card
description: A self-contained card that reflows from stacked to side-by-side based on the width of its parent slot, not the viewport.
usage: Wrap the card in a .cq-slot element (which gets container-type: inline-size) and drop it into any sidebar, modal, or hero — the @container queries in styles.css swap the grid template and type scale based on the slot's width, with no media queries or JavaScript. Put the brand tokens (the .cq-scope block, or your own :root vars) on any ancestor so the colors resolve.
license: web.dev / content under CC-BY 4.0 — reimplemented; container queries are native Baseline CSS

name: CSS Scroll Reveal Timeline
description: Zero-JavaScript clip-path and fade reveals plus a top scroll-progress bar driven entirely by the native CSS animation-timeline view() and scroll() functions.
usage: Include styles.css, drop a single <div class="srt-progress"> near the top of <body> for the scroll bar, then add .srt-reveal plus a variant (.srt-fade-up, .srt-clip, .srt-clip--up, or .srt-zoom) to any element you want revealed. Stagger siblings by setting an inline --srt-delay between 0 and 1.
license: Public-domain CSS idiom — reimplemented; technique is a native CSS feature (no library).

name: CSS-Only Snap Carousel
description: A swipeable, paginated carousel with prev/next buttons and dot markers built with zero JavaScript via scroll-snap plus the new ::scroll-button and ::scroll-marker pseudo-elements.
usage: Copy styles.css into your project and mark up a .snap-carousel wrapper containing a .snap-carousel__track list with one .snap-carousel__slide per item (see index.html). The browser generates the prev/next buttons and dot pagination automatically — no scripts, no extra markup.
license: Public-domain CSS idiom — reimplemented from MDN docs (CC-BY-SA 2.5); CSS Overflow L5 features are native and unencumbered

name: Glassmorphism Card
description: A frosted glass card using backdrop-blur with a subtle light border and an inner top-left highlight.
usage: Copy the markup from index.html and styles.css. Place the card over a photo or gradient background so the backdrop-blur has something to frost.

name: Gooey Blob
description: An organic morphing gooey blob — a border-radius morph variant plus an SVG goo-filter variant that melts moving circles together.
usage: Option A: drop a .scs-blob div for a self-morphing blob (no SVG). Option B: paste the hidden SVG goo filter once, then use .scs-goo with child spans for circles that gooily merge.

name: Gradient Border Glow
description: An element wrapped in an animated rotating conic-gradient border with a soft blurred glow that brightens on hover.
usage: Add class .scs-gradient-border to any container and put content inside. Tune --scs-border-width and --scs-radius; recolor via the conic-gradient stops. Uses @property to animate the angle.

name: Grain / Noise Overlay
description: A fine film-grain texture overlay built from an inline SVG noise data-uri, addable to any section via one class.
usage: Add class .scs-grain to any positioned section. Optional modifiers: .scs-grain--film (heavier) and .scs-grain--animated (flicker).

name: Heart Like Burst
description: A like button where the heart pops with an elastic bounce and a ring of colorful particles bursts outward, with no images or JavaScript.
usage: Copy styles.css into your stylesheet and drop in the .hlb markup (a hidden checkbox plus .hlb__heart and .hlb__glyph spans) for each button. Tune per instance with the --hlb-size, --hlb-liked, --hlb-idle, and --hlb-ring custom properties on the wrapper.
license: CSS-Tricks tutorial by Ana Tudor — technique reimplemented cleanly, shared for learning

name: Infinite Marquee
description: A smooth, seamless infinite horizontal marquee that loops without a jump and pauses on hover.
usage: Duplicate the content group twice inside the track (mark the copy aria-hidden). Tune speed/spacing with the --scs-marquee-duration and --scs-marquee-gap variables; add .scs-marquee--reverse to flip direction.

name: Neon Glow Button
description: A pill button with a layered neon glow (outer halo, ring, inner fill, text glow) that intensifies on hover and focus.
usage: Add class .scs-neon-btn to a <button> or <a>. Change glow color via the --scs-neon variable or the --sand / --violet modifier classes.

name: Retro Synthwave Grid Floor
description: An infinitely scrolling Tron/vaporwave floor grid that recedes to a glowing horizon, built entirely from layered gradients and a single 3D transform with no canvas or JavaScript.
usage: Drop the .rgf markup (sky, sun, plane, grid) into a sized container and include styles.css; the grid fills its parent and scrolls forever. Override the --rgf-* custom properties to retune line color, glow, cell size, speed, tilt, and perspective.
license: MIT — reimplemented from scratch; technique (perspective grid via repeating gradients) is an unencumbered public-domain CSS idiom

name: Shimmer Skeleton
description: Loading placeholder blocks with an animated shimmer sweep, plus shape and width helper classes.
usage: Use .scs-skeleton with a shape helper (--text, --title, --avatar, --thumb, --btn) and optional width helper (--w90/--w75/--w60/--w40). Compose blocks to mirror your real content, then swap in content when loaded.

name: Sliding Underline Link
description: A link underline that wipes in on hover and correctly wraps across multiple lines, using an animated background-size instead of a transform.
usage: Add the styles.css to your stylesheet and apply the .su-link class to any anchor; tune color and thickness per instance with the --su-color and --su-thickness custom properties, or use the --reverse, --bold, and --retract modifiers.
license: CSS { In Real Life } blog (Michelle Barker) — educational snippet, reimplemented cleanly

name: 3D Scroll Text Cylinder
description: Lines of text wrapped around an invisible 3D cylinder that rotates through depth as you scroll, with no WebGL required.
usage: Wrap .cyl-line spans in a [data-cylinder] element inside a .cyl-stage section, then call initScrollCylinder(); tune via data-radius, data-arc, data-spin and data-axis ("x" tube or "y" carousel). ScrollSmoother is optional and auto-detected for inertia.
license: MIT — reimplemented from the Codrops/Tympanus tutorial technique (free for personal and commercial use; GSAP plugins are now free).

name: Gravity Mouse Trail
description: Images burst from the cursor as it moves, then fall under simulated gravity, bounce off the bottom of the viewport, and fade away.
usage: Drop in a positioned .gmt-stage element, then call initGravityMouseTrail(stageEl, { images: [...] }); pass an array of preloaded image URLs and the trail spawns from the cursor on mousemove.
license: Codrops/Tympanus license — free for personal and commercial use, no redistribution as-is. Reimplemented cleanly for saltycodestudio; no physics engine.

name: Horizontal Scroll Gallery
description: Pins a track and translates it horizontally so vertical scrolling sweeps a row of panels sideways across the viewport.
usage: Wrap panels in .hscroll > .hscroll-track > .hscroll-panel and call initHorizontalGallery().

name: Image Scrub Sequence
description: Scrubbing the scroll plays through a frame sequence rendered to canvas (procedurally generated, no external image assets required).
usage: Provide a tall .scrub-section wrapping a pinned <canvas class="scrub-canvas">, then call initScrubSequence().

name: Infinite Parallax Scroll
description: Fullscreen sections that loop endlessly with eased snap, while their inner media drifts at a slower rate to create a seamless sense of depth.
usage: Duplicate your first .ips__section as the last child (tag it data-ips-clone) inside a [data-ips] container, then call initInfiniteParallaxScroll() after GSAP and Lenis load. Lenis infinite:true hides the loop seam, GSAP parallaxes each .ips__media, and Lenis Snap eases to whole-viewport stops.
license: Codrops/Tympanus — reimplemented; demo code free for personal and commercial use, not redistributed as-is.

name: Layered Zoom Scroll
description: A cinematic trailing-zoom hero where stacked image layers scale and de-blur into focus while split headline text parts to reveal a masked central subject on scroll.
usage: Drop the smooth-wrapper/smooth-content scaffold and .lzs hero markup into your page, then call initLayeredZoomScroll() after GSAP loads. Tune layer count, start scales, blur, and word travel via the options object.
license: Codrops tutorial — clean reimplementation; credits original Telescope site authors; GSAP plugins (incl. ScrollSmoother) are now free for everyone.

name: Magnetic Button
description: A button (and its label) is magnetically pulled toward the cursor while hovered and springs back on leave.
usage: Add class .magnetic with an inner .magnetic-label, then call initMagneticButtons().

name: Parallax Layers
description: Multiple depth layers translate at different speeds on scroll to create a sense of dimensional depth.
usage: Give layer elements data-parallax-speed (e.g. -0.3 to 0.6) inside a .parallax-scene and call initParallaxLayers().

name: Pinned Scroll Section
description: Pins a full-height section in place while its inner content animates through distinct stages as the user scrolls past it.
usage: Wrap your section in .pin-section with a .pin-inner and stage elements; call initPinnedSection() after GSAP + ScrollTrigger load.

name: Scroll Progress Bar
description: A slim fixed bar at the top of the page that fills from 0 to 100% as the user scrolls through the document.
usage:
Add a
at the top of body and call initScrollProgress().

name: Scroll Text Reveal
description: Lines or words rise up and fade in with a stagger as each block enters the viewport.
usage: Add data-reveal (optionally data-reveal="words") to text elements and call initScrollReveal().

name: Scroll Velocity Skew Marquee
description: An infinite horizontal marquee that skews and stretches in proportion to scroll velocity, snapping back to rest when the scroll stops.
usage: Import initScrollVelocitySkewMarquee, pass it a wrapper element containing a [data-svm-track] row with two identical sets of items, and the marquee loops infinitely while leaning into your scroll velocity. Include styles.css for layout and reduced-motion handling.
license: Inspired by an official GreenSock CodePen; reimplemented cleanly. GSAP core is free under the standard GreenSock 'no charge' license.

name: Split Text Stagger
description: Splits a heading into characters or words in plain JS and staggers them into view (no paid SplitText plugin required).
usage: Add data-split ("chars" or "words") to a heading and call initSplitStagger(); fires on scroll into view.

name: Sticky Grid Scroll
description: A pinned 3-column image grid that staggers in, scales and opens up, and reveals an overlaid title and CTA at precise scroll points before releasing.
usage: Mark up .sgs > .sgs-stage > (.sgs-grid with three .sgs-col / .sgs-cell columns + a [data-sgs-content] overlay), include styles.css, then call initStickyGridScroll(). Lenis is auto-detected; pass { lenis: false } to opt out.
license: Inspired by a Codrops/Tympanus tutorial (free for personal & commercial use) — reimplemented cleanly, no verbatim source.

name: Sticky Stacking Cards
description: A stack of cards where each pins in place and slightly scales back as the next card slides up and covers it on scroll.
usage: Wrap .stack-card items in a .stack-cards container and call initStackingCards().

name: SVG Line Draw on Scroll
description: An SVG path that progressively draws itself in sync with scroll, ideal for connecting timeline sections or tracing illustrations.
usage: Add an SVG with class draw-on-scroll containing stroked fill:none paths, include styles.css + GSAP/ScrollTrigger + animation.js, then call initSvgLineDraw() (optionally scoped with pathSelector/trigger/start/end).
license: GSAP + DrawSVGPlugin are now free under the standard GSAP license; this is an original reimplementation using the stroke-dashoffset idiom on core GSAP. Pure-CSS scroll-timeline variant is an unrestricted public-domain idiom. MIT — reimplemented.

name: SVG Text Clip Reveal
description: Large display type used as an SVG clip-path that wipes open on scroll to reveal an image or pattern sliding behind the letters.
usage: Include styles.css and animation.js, register GSAP + ScrollTrigger, and add a [data-stcr] section whose SVG has a <clipPath> wrapping the text and a media layer clipped to it. animation.js auto-inits on DOMContentLoaded; call initSvgTextClipReveal(opts) manually to tune drift/scrub.
license: Inspired by Codrops/Tympanus demo; reimplemented from scratch. Codrops license: free for personal and commercial use, no redistribution as-is.

name: Animated Beam Connector
description: An animated gradient pulse that travels along a curved SVG path connecting two referenced DOM nodes, ideal for integration and architecture diagrams.
usage: Give a relative container a ref, give each node you want to wire its own ref, then render one <AnimatedBeam containerRef fromRef toRef /> per connection; tune curvature, reverse, duration, delay and the gradient colours, and the path auto-recomputes on resize via a ResizeObserver.
license: MIT (Magic UI, github.com/magicuidesign/magicui) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Animated Counter
description: A number that eases up to a target value when it scrolls into view, with prefix/suffix and locale formatting.
usage: Use <AnimatedCounter value={1200} suffix='+' /> for a single stat, or <StatGrid /> for the sample row.

name: Bento Grid
description: A responsive asymmetric bento grid of feature cards with a subtle hover-lift and glow.
usage: Import BentoGrid and pass an items array, or use the default Sand & Surf sample content.

name: Border Beam
description: An animated beam of light that continuously travels around the border of any container, framing cards and pricing tiers with a premium glow.
usage: Drop <BorderBeam /> inside any relative + overflow-hidden, rounded container to frame it with a travelling glow; tune colorFrom/colorTo, duration, delay, reverse and initialOffset, and stack two beams with offset delays for a chasing effect.
license: MIT (Magic UI, github.com/magicuidesign/magicui) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Canvas Particle Field
description: Lightweight canvas particles that drift and gently react to the cursor, adding depth and motion behind hero content.
usage: Render <CanvasParticleField /> as the first child of a position:relative hero section so it sits absolutely behind your content. Tune quantity, size, color, vx/vy drift, staticity, and ease to dial in the depth and mouse responsiveness.
license: MIT — reimplemented (inspired by Magic UI, magicuidesign/magicui)

name: Command Palette
description: A ⌘K-style command palette modal with fuzzy filtering, keyboard navigation, and grouped commands.
usage: Render <CommandPalette commands={...} /> anywhere; press ⌘K / Ctrl+K to open. Pass your own commands array.

name: Confetti Button
description: A button that bursts confetti from its own position on click to celebrate signups, purchases and other success moments.
usage: Render <ConfettiButton>Sign up</ConfettiButton> wherever you want a celebratory click; on press it reads its own bounding rect, normalises the centre to viewport-origin coordinates and fires canvas-confetti from that exact spot. Tune particleCount, spread, angle, startVelocity, gravity, scalar and colors, and use onConfetti for follow-up logic.
license: MIT (Magic UI; wraps MIT canvas-confetti) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Dark Mode Toggle
description: An accessible animated theme toggle that morphs a sun into a moon and persists the choice to localStorage.
usage: Render <DarkModeToggle />; it toggles the `dark` class on <html> and remembers the preference.

name: Feature Accordion
description: A single-open accordion of features with smooth grid-based height animation and accessible disclosure semantics.
usage: Render <FeatureAccordion items={[...]} /> or use the built-in sample features.

name: Gradient Mesh Hero
description: A hero section with an animated gradient-mesh blob background, grain overlay, and a bold headline.
usage: Render <GradientMeshHero /> at the top of a page; pass eyebrow/title/subtitle/CTA props to customize.

name: Hover Glow Border
description: A Cursor-style border glow that orbits any card and concentrates toward the mouse pointer, adapting to any container size.
usage: Wrap any card or panel in <HoverGlowBorder> and give the inner element a matching rounded background; tune spread, proximity, inactiveZone and movementDuration to shape how tightly the glow chases the cursor.
license: MIT (Aceternity UI) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Lamp Effect
description: A Linear-inspired overhead lamp glow that fans light down onto a section header, with the headline rising into the beam on scroll.
usage: Render <LampEffect title="..." subtitle="..." /> as a section header; pass a `glow` color to retint the beam and optional children for CTAs.
license: MIT (Aceternity UI) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Logo Marquee
description: An infinite horizontal marquee of client/partner logos with edge fade and pause-on-hover.
usage: Render <LogoMarquee logos={[...]} /> with text or node logos; defaults to sample wordmarks.

name: macOS Dock
description: A macOS-style icon dock whose items magnify and lift as the cursor approaches, for portfolio nav bars and app launchers.
usage: Wrap a row of <DockItem label="..."> icons in <MacosDock>; the dock tracks the cursor's X position and springs each icon's size so neighbours scale in a smooth bell curve around the hovered icon. Tune baseSize, maxSize, and distance props to taste.
license: MIT (Magic UI) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Pricing Toggle
description: Pricing cards with a monthly/annual switch that animates the displayed price and shows annual savings.
usage: Render <PricingToggle plans={...} /> or use the built-in sample tiers.

name: Shrinking Sticky Navbar
description: A sticky navbar that condenses its height and gains a backdrop blur once the page is scrolled.
usage: Render <ShrinkingStickyNavbar /> at the top of your layout; it manages its own scroll listener.

name: Spotlight Card
description: A card that reveals a soft radial spotlight following the cursor on hover, ideal for premium-but-safe feature and pricing grids.
usage: Import SpotlightCard and pass title/description/icon (or your own children); arrange several in a grid for feature or pricing layouts. Move the cursor over a card to reveal the spotlight.
license: MIT (Aceternity UI) — reimplemented with credit

name: Testimonial Carousel
description: An auto-advancing testimonial slider with dot navigation, pause-on-hover, and smooth fade/slide transitions.
usage: Render <TestimonialCarousel testimonials={...} /> or use the built-in sample quotes.

name: Text Shimmer
description: Text with a soft light sheen sweeping across it left to right, perfect for announcement pills, badges and subtle loading labels.
usage: Import TextShimmer and wrap any short string, e.g. <TextShimmer>Now in beta</TextShimmer> inside a pill, or set as="label" with a longer duration for a subtle loading label. Tune duration, spread, baseColor and shineColor via props.
license: MIT (Magic UI) — reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: WebGL Mesh Gradient Plasma
description: A flowing WebGL mesh-gradient of color spots that swirl and distort like plasma, for a high-end animated hero canvas.
usage: Wrap your hero content in <MeshGradientPlasma> to lay a live GLSL plasma canvas behind it; tune colors, speed, distortion, swirl, grainMixer and grainOverlay to taste. It freezes on a still frame automatically when prefers-reduced-motion is set.
license: PolyForm Shield — free for commercial/non-commercial use unless it competes with Paper; wrapper code reimplemented cleanly with credit

name: Copy to Clipboard
description: A copy button that uses the async Clipboard API (with a legacy fallback) and shows an animated "Copied!" confirmation state.
usage: Add a button with data-copy="text" or data-copy-target="#selector". script.js handles copying and the confirmation state automatically.

name: Custom Cursor
description: A custom cursor with a precise dot and a lerp-trailing ring that grows and changes over links and buttons; hides the native cursor and disables itself on touch devices.
usage:
Link styles.css and script.js, add
to the page. Mark interactive elements with [data-cursor] or rely on a/button auto-detection.

name: Modal Dialog
description: An accessible modal dialog with focus trap, Esc-to-close, backdrop-click close, body scroll lock, and a fade/scale-in animation.
usage: Add the modal markup, give triggers data-modal-open="<id>". script.js wires open/close, focus trapping and scroll lock automatically.

name: Preloader
description: A polished full-screen preloader with an animated count-up and progress sweep that slides away once the page has finished loading.
usage: Paste the preloader markup as the first child of <body>, link styles.css and script.js. It removes itself on window load; reveals page content via a body class.

name: Scrollspy Nav
description: A navigation that highlights the current section using IntersectionObserver and smooth-scrolls to anchors on click.
usage: Give nav links href="#section-id" and a data-scrollspy attribute on the nav. Sections need matching ids. script.js observes them and toggles .is-active.

name: Smooth Scroll
description: Lerp-based smooth (inertia) page scrolling driven by requestAnimationFrame, with automatic opt-out for prefers-reduced-motion and touch devices.
usage:
Link styles.css and script.js. Wrap page content in
...
. Disable by removing the script or via prefers-reduced-motion.

name: Tabs
description: Accessible tabs with full ARIA roles and arrow-key navigation, plus a sliding active indicator that animates between tabs.
usage: Use the tablist/tab/tabpanel markup with matching ids and aria-controls. script.js handles selection, keyboard nav and the moving indicator.

name: Theme Switcher
description: A light/dark theme toggle built on CSS variables and a data-theme attribute that persists to localStorage and respects the OS prefers-color-scheme.
usage: Add the inline no-flash snippet in <head>, a button with id="theme-toggle", then link styles.css and script.js. Build your UI with the provided CSS variables.
